questions.question: What does the abbreviation LAN stand for?
questions.explanation: LAN stands for Local Area Network — a network covering a small area such as a home or office.

questions.question: Which protocol is used to assign IP addresses automatically?
questions.explanation: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) leases IP addresses to clients automatically. DNS resolves names, FTP transfers files, SNMP monitors devices.

questions.question: Which of the following are transport layer protocols?
questions.explanation: TCP and UDP are layer-4 transport protocols. IP is a network-layer protocol and HTTP is an application-layer protocol.

questions.question: What kind of attack floods a service with traffic to make it unavailable?
questions.explanation: A Denial of Service (DoS) attack overwhelms a service with traffic so legitimate users cannot reach it.

questions.question: Which measures help to secure a Wi-Fi network?
questions.explanation: WPA3 encryption and a strong pre-shared key protect a Wi-Fi network. Broadcasting the admin password or disabling encryption do the opposite.

questions.question: Sort each protocol by the transport layer it runs on. One item is not a transport protocol at all — leave it in the tray.
questions.explanation: HTTP and SSH need the reliable, connection-oriented delivery of TCP. DHCP and TFTP use the lightweight, connectionless UDP. HTML is a markup language, not a transport protocol, so it belongs in neither basket.

questions.question: Put the steps of establishing a TCP connection (the three-way handshake) in the correct order.

answers.text: The client sends a SYN segment to the server.
The server replies with a SYN-ACK segment.
The client sends an ACK segment back to the server.
The client sends a FIN segment to close the connection.
The server floods the client with unsolicited data.

questions.explanation: TCP opens a connection with a three-way handshake: SYN, then SYN-ACK, then ACK. A FIN closes an existing connection, and unsolicited flooding is not part of the handshake.

questions.question: For each statement about transport protocols, decide whether it is true (yes) or false (no).

answers.text: TCP uses a three-way handshake to establish a connection.
UDP has a higher per-packet overhead than TCP.

questions.explanation: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable, opening connections with a three-way handshake. UDP is connectionless, does not guarantee delivery or ordering, and has less overhead than TCP.

questions.question: Choose the correct answer in each selectbox.

selectboxes.label: Protocol used to browse secure websites:

questions.explanation: HTTPS secures web traffic and listens on port 443 by default. FTP uses port 21 and SMTP uses port 25.
